aAbout: Sentinel Hub is a cloud-based service providing easy access to global archives of analysis-ready Earth observation data from the major providers. Its documentation lists seven APIs — Processing, Batch Processing, Bring Your Own COG, Catalog, Third Party Data Import, Statistical and OGC — covering the Sentinels (including Sentinel-1, Sentinel-2, Sentinel-3 and Sentinel-5P), Landsat, commercial Planet PlanetScope and Maxar collections, elevation models and more, plus bring-your-own-data collections and custom scripting. EO Browser is described in its documentation as a free web application that showcases the service — search, view, analyse and download data on the fly. An account is required for API use, and paid subscriptions are metered in processing units.
aStrengths: Sentinel Hub is the genuine professional platform: seven documented APIs that process satellite imagery in the cloud without you building or managing infrastructure, configurable band maths and custom scripts, multi-temporal and statistical analysis, bring-your-own-data collections, and a catalogue spanning the Sentinels, Landsat, Planet and Maxar. For developers, researchers and GIS teams who need programmatic, scalable Earth-observation pipelines — in their own environment or in Sentinel Hub's cloud GIS — it is the industrial tool, and EO Browser gives anyone a free way to see what the data can do.
bAbout: Zoom Earth is, in its own terms, an interactive weather map of the world and a real-time hurricane tracker, provided by Neave Interactive Limited. Live satellite images from NOAA GOES, JMA Himawari and EUMETSAT Meteosat geostationary satellites are updated every 10 minutes, with HD images updated twice a day from NASA polar-orbiting satellites Aqua and Terra. Around that imagery it layers a rain radar with nowcasting, forecast maps from DWD ICON and NOAA GFS models (precipitation, wind, temperature, pressure and more), hurricane tracking using NHC, JTWC, NRL and IBTrACS data, and wildfire heat spots from NASA FIRMS. It runs on the web and as iOS and Android apps, and no account is required for basic use — an account is optional and carries a Pro subscription across devices.
bStrengths: Zoom Earth is the better pure weather experience, and it is not close: near real-time satellite imagery every 10 minutes from three geostationary fleets, twice-daily HD passes from Aqua and Terra, rain radar with nowcasting, a full set of forecast-model maps, best-in-class hurricane tracking, and wildfire heat spots — all free, with no account required, in a focused interface on web, iPhone, iPad and Android. If a storm is the story, its single-purpose design beats any generalist tool for speed and depth.
betterAnswer: They solve different problems. Sentinel Hub is a developer platform: analysis-ready satellite data from Sentinel, Landsat, Planet and Maxar, processed in the cloud through seven APIs and paid for in processing units, with no public price list and a 30-day free trial. Zoom Earth is a consumer weather map: free, no account needed, with satellite imagery every 10 minutes, rain radar and hurricane tracking on web and mobile apps, and no API at all. If you want to *build with* satellite data, use Sentinel Hub; if you want to *watch the weather* from space, open Zoom Earth.

intro: Sentinel Hub and Zoom Earth both show you the Earth from space, and that is almost where the resemblance ends. Sentinel Hub, run by Sinergise, a Planet Labs company, is a cloud platform for developers and researchers: seven APIs that search, process, analyse and download analysis-ready satellite data, metered in processing units, with the free EO Browser as its showcase viewer. Zoom Earth, by Neave Interactive, is a consumer weather map anyone can open for free: live satellite imagery updated every 10 minutes, rain radar, forecast maps and a hurricane tracker, on the web and in iOS and Android apps.
pricingA: No public price is published for Sentinel Hub. Its pricing page redirects to Planet pricing with contact-sales options and no Sentinel Hub plan prices listed, so no euro or dollar figure can be confirmed from official public pages. What is published is the structure: paid subscriptions metered in processing units (PU), with the official FAQ giving allowances of 30,000 PU per month for Exploration (which does not support commercial use), up to 70,000 PU per month for Basic, and 400,000 PU per month for Enterprise S, plus a top-up package of 50,000 PU. A 30-day free trial gives API-level access, and EO Browser is a free showcase application.
pricingB: Zoom Earth is free on the web and its apps are listed at 0 USD on the App Store and Google Play, with an optional auto-renewable Zoom Earth Pro subscription for more features. The official US App Store listing shows two Zoom Earth Pro price points — $1.99 and $11.99 — under in-app purchases, but the listing checked does not label which billing period each price corresponds to, so the period for either price is unverified. No free trial for Pro was stated on the official pages checked, and no separate pricing page was found on zoom.earth itself — pricing is surfaced through the app stores.

verdictA: Choose Sentinel Hub if you are building with satellite data — an application, a research pipeline, a GIS workflow — and need analysis-ready imagery, custom processing and statistics through an API, metered in processing units after a 30-day free trial.
verdictB: Choose Zoom Earth if you want to watch the weather itself — a developing hurricane, a rain front, smoke from a fire — in near real time, for free, with nothing to set up and no account needed.
verdictLine: Sentinel Hub is the workshop — satellite data as a programmable, metered cloud service for people who build things with it. Zoom Earth is the window — the same planet as a free, live weather picture for people who want to watch it. One is priced in processing units with no public price list; the other is free with an optional app-store Pro tier.
worldEye: Neither of these helps you look at a place on the ground, and that is the gap WorldEye fills: a hosted 3D globe that opens free in any browser with no signup — 74,229 public cameras across 109 countries, alongside live flights, ships, satellites, weather, earthquakes and wildfires in the same view. WorldEye is not a processing platform like Sentinel Hub — it offers no Earth-observation API pipeline or processing units — and it is not a dedicated storm tool like Zoom Earth, whose radar and hurricane depth it does not match. Its Pro tier is $7.99/week, $13.99/month or $74.99/year for viewers who want more of the globe, not a data pipeline.
